An inspiring atmosphere and interdisciplinary collaboration at eye level await you on the modern campus in Nottwil. Some of the team are already in the flow, others are arriving comfortably. You listen, ask the right questions and transform wishes into realistic, implementable solutions. As a link between IT and specialist departments, you are a translator, an enabler and sometimes also a gentle representative of reality - always with a smile. 11:00 - In a call with an external partner you keep track of things. Releases, adjustments, tests – you document decisions and ensure that everyone knows what, why and how is being implemented. Transparency and traceability are a given for you. 12:00 - Lunch break. Some take a walk in the sun, others go to the swimming pool, some philosophize over coffee. Everything can, nothing has to. The main thing is to clear your head. 13:00 - Further development and operation of your applications. You accompany changes, test new functions, approve them and document them. No chaos, no "only two people know", but sustainable solutions that can be understood later - even on a Monday morning. 3:00 p.m. - Support requests? No problem! The service desk is the first point of contact, you are the escalation and resolution authority. You analyze, prioritize, bring order to the topic and coordinate with internal professionals from IT and other areas. You take responsibility and prefer to solve tickets yourself instead of forwarding them. 4:30 p.m. - Project time is in the late afternoon. You prioritize, coordinate, engage stakeholders and define the next steps. You think ahead so that challenges don't arise in the first place - and bring everyone involved together. Together you discuss requirements, plan updates and initiate further developments. 5:30 p.m. - Closing time. The systems run stably, open points are clear and perhaps there is a short exchange within the team – professionally or privately. There is space for both. And sometimes we toast the day's successes together, with an aperitif of course! What sets you apart
• You have training in the field of business informatics - regardless of whether your path was traditional or lateral.
• Administrative applications are valuable, well thought-out systems for you with logic, rules and dependencies. You understand how they work, where they react sensitively and why seemingly small adjustments often have a big impact. Accordingly, you already have experience in application management - ideally in the area of ​​time recording, cash register systems or PowerApps.
• You leave the writing of code to the professionals, but you understand enough technology to be able to think along, discuss and take part. When someone talks about releases, dependencies or “small adjustments with a big impact,” you don’t just nod politely, you know what they mean.
• Communication is a central part of your work for you. You like to talk to the departments, listen, ask questions and explain clearly - without technical jargon and without IT abbreviation bingo.
• For you, team is more than just a buzzword for presentations. You enjoy working with others, sharing knowledge, helping and even asking for help yourself. Good solutions arise for you through exchange – when we think together, discuss things and sometimes laugh together. Releases, Anpassungen, Tests – du dokumentierst Entscheidungen und sorgst dafür, dass alle wissen, was, warum und wie umgesetzt wird. Gemeinsam besprecht ihr Anforderungen, plant Updates und setzt Weiterentwicklungen in Gang. 17:30 - Feierabend. Die Systeme laufen stabil, offene Punkte sind klar und vielleicht gibt's noch einen kurzen Austausch im Team – fachlich oder privat. Beides hat Platz.
